clue.text: It sounds horny having a bath first

indicators.note: tells us the bath comes before the a, though the clue names it second

parts.note: a tub is a bathtub, a bath

explanation.surface: A cheeky line about someone feeling amorous after a soak in the tub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horny' tempts as slang for aroused; here it means sounding like a horn, which a big brass instrument does.
explanation.definitionFit: The instrument is the deepest member of the brass family, so its sound is literally horn-like.

clue.text: Take up unfinished puzzle — one way to get a lift

definitions.text: one way to get a lift

indicators.note: in a down clue, taking something up means reading it from the bottom upward, backwards
the puzzle word loses its final letter, so it is left incomplete

parts.note: a rebus is a picture puzzle

explanation.surface: Someone gives up a half-done puzzle and goes looking for a ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' cuts REBUS to REBU, and 'Take up' turns REBU round to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Uber is a ride-hailing app, so booking through it is one means of getting a ride, called a lift in British English.

clue.text: Wanting a sort of clue Tramp gets to pick

indicators.note: a sort of something is a variant version, so the letters of clue and Tramp get rearranged
wanting means lacking, so the letter named next is missing from the mix

explanation.surface: A tramp is handed some sort of clue and has to make a choice.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of CLUE TRAMP, remove the A that is 'Wanting', and rearrange the remaining eight. 'Pick' looks like a verb meaning choose; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A plectrum is the small flat tool a guitarist uses to strike the strings, commonly called a pick.

clue.text: Chill with old American dope and a drink

parts.note: ice is used to chill things, and ice as a verb means to chill
tea was old American slang for marijuana

explanation.surface: Someone cools off with some vintage American weed and a beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: Iced or ice tea is a cold beverage of sweetened tea served over ice.

clue.text: Gig endlessly securing some money to get a bloody organ

indicators.note: the combined word loses its last letter, so it has no end
securing means holding, so the money sits inside the gig word

parts.note: a gig is a performance, as is a play
a cent is a small sum of money

explanation.surface: A musician's cut-short gig earns a little cash, then turns into something gory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims the gig word only after the money is inside it, so the cut falls on the whole combination, not on the gig alone.
explanation.definitionFit: The placenta is the blood-rich organ that nourishes a foetus in the womb and is delivered after birth.

clue.text: Manifestations of masculinity are mostly, apparently, dormant

indicators.note: apparently signals that being dormant is read as being in beds, so the trimmed word goes inside

parts.note: dormant suggests being asleep, and sleepers lie in their beds

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all of the word are, so its final letter goes

explanation.surface: A claim that signs of manliness are, it seems, largely asleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apparently, dormant' is read cryptically: to be dormant is to be asleep, that is, tucked up in bed, so the shortened 'are' is put to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Facial hair grows on men and is a classic outward sign of maleness.

clue.text: Rumpy-pumpy seen in main City gathering

indicators.note: gathering suggests pulling the letters together into a new heap, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some hanky-panky spotted at a big gathering in the City of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rumpy-pumpy' is jokey British slang for sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Intimacy is a polite euphemism for sexual relations, which the jokey phrase describes.

clue.text: State so petty to convince of lie?

parts.note: GA is the abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
petty means slight, trivial

explanation.surface: A question whether a country is being small-minded enough to deceive people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a verb meaning declare, but it is the US state Georgia.
explanation.definitionFit: To manipulate someone psychologically into doubting their own perception, as in the play and film, is to make them believe a falsehood.

clue.text: I, with no end of human brilliance, managed to develop a stomach bulge

indicators.note: the letters are worked into a new form, as if developed into something else
the word human loses its final letter, leaving no end

explanation.surface: Someone boasts that, with endless human genius, they managed to grow a paunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end of' looks like 'plenty of', but it cuts HUMAN to HUMA; I, HUMA and BRILLIANCE are then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a protrusion of the intestine through the abdominal wall at the navel, seen as a swelling of the belly.

clue.text: Orange-coloured American advertising one retirement option?

parts.note: PR, public relations, is publicity work
I is the Roman numeral one
retiring is going to bed, and a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: An American advertising someone's choice of pension scheme, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement option' suggests pensions; here retiring means going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: The fruit gives its name to a pale yellowish-orange shade, so the word serves as a colour adjective.

clue.text: Pushers might supply these in piano bars

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
rods are bars

explanation.surface: Drug dealers might sell their wares in piano bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pushers' suggests drug dealers; the word means anyone or anything that pushes, and pokes are what they deliver.
explanation.definitionFit: A prod is a poke or nudge, which is exactly what something that pushes gives.

clue.text: It's my call to be affectionate

parts.note: cor and my are both British exclamations of surprise
to dial is to call on the telephone

explanation.surface: A speaker announces that it is their decision to be loving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my' looks like a possessive; it is the exclamation 'My!', which the British 'Cor!' matches.
explanation.definitionFit: Cordial means warm and friendly in manner, a mild form of affection.

clue.text: What kind of beast would abuse and rob men?

indicators.note: to abuse words is to mistreat them, so these letters get mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A question about which animal would attack and mug people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abuse' reads as a verb in a list with 'rob', but it signals rearranging AND ROB MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: This German breed of guard dog has a fearsome reputation, the sort of creature imagined attacking robbers.

clue.text: Drunks' language is filled with vernacular

indicators.note: the phrase drunks' language contains the answer within its letters, running across the two words

explanation.surface: A remark that the way drunks talk is full of everyday speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang is informal everyday speech, the kind of local idiom that vernacular describes.

clue.text: Feigns hesitation when surrounded by fools

indicators.note: the hesitation sound sits within the fools word

parts.note: asses are fools
um is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone pretends to dither when hemmed in by idiots.
explanation.definitionFit: To assume an air or manner is to put it on falsely, which is to feign it.

clue.text: Drink promotion briefly uttered raising cheers

parts.note: an ad is a promotion, an advertisement

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: vocal means spoken aloud, uttered

indicators.note: in a down clue raising means lifting the word so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, as is cheers

explanation.surface: A drinks advert is spoken in brief, raising a toast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' trims VOCAL to VOCA; 'raising' turns TA upward to AT.
explanation.definitionFit: Advocaat is a Dutch liqueur made with eggs, sugar and brandy, a sweet alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Vessels following stars reach idyllic destinations

indicators.note: following means the vessels word comes after the stars word

parts.note: suns are stars
pots are vessels, containers

explanation.surface: Ships steered by the stars arrive at paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessels' suggests ships, but here they are pots.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunspots are sunny holiday places, the kind of perfect resort a traveller dreams about.

clue.text: Unpleasant relations hurt, according to Spooner

indicators.note: Spooner, famous for swapping the starts of words, signals exchanging their opening sounds

parts.note: kin are relations, family
to sting is to hurt

explanation.surface: A complaint that family members were nasty and wounding.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of KIN and STING to get STIN and KING.
explanation.definitionFit: Stinking, meaning foul or very nasty, describes something thoroughly disagreeable.

clue.text: She treats good person after obsessive year

indicators.note: after means the saint comes at the end, behind the obsessive and the year

parts.note: anal, short for anal-retentive, means obsessively fussy
ST, saint, is a holy good person

explanation.surface: A woman cares for a kind man after a year of compulsive behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She treats' is a person who treats patients, a psychoanalyst.
explanation.definitionFit: A psychoanalyst is a therapist whose job is treating patients' minds.

clue.text: A conservative old American jerk with no power

parts.note: US, United States, means American
a tic is an involuntary twitch or jerk

explanation.surface: A description of an elderly Tory American as an idiot without influence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no power' looks like part of the insult; it is the definition, in the sense of an unplugged instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: An acoustic guitar is played without electrical amplification, so it needs no electricity.

clue.text: Jerk regularly serves up weak hashish

indicators.note: in a down clue, serving up means bringing the letters upward, so they read backwards
regularly means taking every other letter, here the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: A lout keeps dealing feeble cannabis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of 'weak hashish', EKAHS, and 'serves up' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: A shake is a sudden jolt or jerk of movement.

clue.text: 'Taste of Heaven' used as embodiment of love

indicators.note: a taste is a small part, so only a portion of the phrase is taken, spanning both words

explanation.surface: A product called Taste of Heaven is advertised as love personified.
explanation.definitionFit: Venus is the Roman goddess of love, so she is the personification of that emotion.

clue.text: Curious dog

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the beagle in the Peanuts comic strip

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a single odd dog; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Snoopy means prying into others' affairs, and is also the name of Charlie Brown's cartoon beagle.

clue.text: I love millions expanding in offshore financial centre

parts.note: I, plus O for love (zero in tennis) and M for millions, make IOM, the standard abbreviation of the island, which is then written out in full

explanation.surface: A boast of loving the way millions grow in a tax haven.
explanation.walkthrough: I, O and M are the island's abbreviation; 'expanding' means writing that abbreviation out as the full name. It is a Crown dependency in the Irish Sea, known as a low-tax haven.
explanation.definitionFit: The island has its own low tax regime and is a well-known tax haven for banking and investment.

clue.text: After party, the Spanish soprano is slurring

indicators.note: after means the Spanish word and the singer follow the party word

parts.note: LIB is short for the Liberal party
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: After a party, a Spanish opera singer is slurring her words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slurring' suggests drunken speech; it means smearing someone's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To slur someone is to make damaging false statements about them, which is what libelling does.

clue.text: Rubbish bags for geological feature

indicators.note: bags means holds, so the for word is held inside the rubbish word

parts.note: cack is British slang for rubbish or excrement
pro means for, in favour of

explanation.surface: Bin liners used to carry stone, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bags' looks like a plural noun; it is a verb meaning holds.
explanation.definitionFit: Caprock is a hard layer of rock capping softer strata, a feature studied by geologists.

clue.text: Vicious to stuff workers as well

indicators.note: stuffing means filling, so the punk's first name is packed inside the workers word

parts.note: worker bees, so bees are workers
Sid Vicious was the Sex Pistols' bassist

explanation.surface: A spiteful plan to cram employees, too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vicious' looks like an adjective; it is the surname of punk musician Sid Vicious, standing for SID.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides means in addition, also, too.

clue.text: Double Dutch: A tip for lookers!

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter, here of lookers

explanation.surface: A mock tip-off about double Dutch from the setter Dutch for the good-looking.
explanation.walkthrough: Dutch is also the setter's pseudonym, which adds a wink to 'Double Dutch'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dual means twofold, having two parts, so it is a synonym for double.

clue.text: Worry about stitch in time? On the contrary

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another
says the order is swapped, so time goes inside stitch rather than stitch inside time

parts.note: to sew is to stitch

explanation.surface: A fret about the saying 'a stitch in time saves nine', turned on its head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stitch in time' reads as the proverb; 'On the contrary' flips it so T goes inside SEW.
explanation.definitionFit: To stew is to fret anxiously, as in stewing over a problem.

clue.text: At end of bar two merry men put ale in teat

indicators.note: merry means tipsy, so the letters reel into a new order

explanation.surface: Two tipsy men at closing time pour ale into a teat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' means except: the definition is 'at the end, except for two', third from last.
explanation.definitionFit: Antepenultimate means third from last, the position at the end but for two.
